blocks.orig: Zanzibar is part of the Zanzibar Archipelago together with Pemba Island and many other smaller islands. Zanzibar Island offers a laidback beach life, but also a large variety of activities, a colorful culture and a deep history. You can go on a spice tour or explore the amazing coral reefs and swim among tropical reef fish.  Zanzibar Island has all the ingredients to make a memorable holiday. See below for our personal top three accommodations as well as our top Zanzibar island itineraries.
blocks.html: Together with Pemba Island and a host of smaller islands, Zanzibar forms the Zanzibar Archipelago. On Zanzibar Island you get relaxed beach living alongside a wide choice of activities, a vibrant culture and a rich history. Join a spice tour, or head out to the stunning coral reefs and swim among tropical reef fish. Everything you need for a holiday to remember is here on Zanzibar Island. Below you'll find our own top three places to stay, plus our favourite Zanzibar island itineraries.

blocks.orig:
Zanzibar island has several beaches and resorts in all four cardinal directions. But our personal preference is the east coast of Zanzibar, mainly because of its gorgeous and serene beaches, the many activities it offers and the various multi-cuisine restaurants, satisfying even the most picky taste palette. According to our travel experts, this side of the island offers you the overall best Zanzibarian experience. Since there are countless of resorts and lodges, we have narrowed our three personal favorites down to three price categories.
For the Silver category, we recommend Fun Beach hotel – 42 rooms with pool or beach view and modern amenities for maximum comfort. For our Gold category, we refer you to Next Paradise – an ocean facing boutique resort with 25 elegantly furnished rooms and excellent dining. The rooms come in several categories with each its own special features.
And last but not least, for our Platinum category (drumroll….. ) – Qambani Luxury Resort. This resort offers the most beautiful and decadent stay in Zanzibar with impeccable service within its six, uniquely themed villas. The refined and graceful strokes in the interior designs and artworks makes each villa tell its own story and still give it a home-away-from-home-feel. Qambani is luxury and comfort at its best!
blocks.html:
Beaches and resorts can be found on every side of Zanzibar island, north, south, east and west. Our own favourite, though, is the east coast, chiefly for its beautiful, tranquil beaches, the wide range of activities and the many restaurants serving all kinds of cuisine, enough to please even the fussiest eater. In the view of our travel experts, this part of the island gives you the best all-round Zanzibar experience. With so many resorts and lodges to choose from, we have narrowed our three personal favourites down to three price categories.
In the Silver category our pick is Fun Beach hotel – 42 rooms with pool or beach view and modern amenities for maximum comfort. In the Gold category we point you to Next Paradise – a boutique resort facing the ocean, with 25 elegantly furnished rooms and excellent food. The rooms are divided into several categories, each with its own special touches.
Finally, in the Platinum category (drumroll….. ) – Qambani Luxury Resort. With flawless service across its six individually themed villas, this resort offers the most beautiful and indulgent stay on Zanzibar. Thanks to the refined, elegant touches in the interiors and artwork, every villa tells a story of its own while still feeling like a home away from home. Qambani is luxury and comfort at their very best!

blocks.orig: The Zanzibar islands are named the Spice Islands, because of their rich history in spice trade and the many spice plantations. The historic Stone Town is an amazing mix of cultures. Food lovers and culture enthusiasts can visit interesting places, such as the Sultan’s Palace, the House of Wonders and the Darajani or Forodhani food markets. The opportunities are truly endless here!
blocks.html: The Zanzibar islands are known as the Spice Islands, a name earned through their long history of spice trading and their many spice plantations. Historic Stone Town is a fascinating blend of cultures, where food lovers and culture enthusiasts can explore spots such as the Sultan's Palace, the House of Wonders and the Darajani and Forodhani food markets. There really is no end to what you can do here!

blocks.orig: Spice tour: walk with a guide through spice plantations where pepper, cinnamon, ginger, cloves, nutmeg and fruit grows.
blocks.html: Spice tour: walk with a guide between plantations where pepper, cinnamon, ginger, cloves, nutmeg and fruit are grown.

blocks.orig: Kitesurfing: at the beaches Paje, Kiwengwa en Nungwi.
blocks.html: Kitesurfing: on the beaches of Paje, Kiwengwa and Nungwi.

blocks.orig: Stone Town excursion: stroll through the narrow streets of this lively town and visit some local markets and the former slave market.
blocks.html: Stone Town excursion: wander the narrow lanes of this bustling town, taking in a few local markets and the former slave market.

blocks.orig: Prison Island excursion: take a 30 minute boat trip to this island, which once was a place where slaves were detained. Nowadays it is  a nature reserve for giant tortoises and a place to see the ruins of the former prison.
blocks.html: Prison Island excursion: a 30 minute boat ride brings you to this island, once used to hold slaves. Today it serves as a nature reserve for giant tortoises, and you can also see the ruins of the old prison.

blocks.orig: Safari Blue: during this excursion you visit 3 islands where you can swim, snorkel and have a nice BBQ.
blocks.html: Safari Blue: an excursion to 3 islands with time to swim, snorkel and enjoy a tasty BBQ.

blocks.orig: Visit Jozani forest: a great jungle walk through the last indigenous forest on Zanzibar with lots of monkeys, like the rare red colobus monkeys.
blocks.html: Jozani forest visit: a wonderful jungle walk through Zanzibar's last remaining native forest, home to plenty of monkeys, including the rare red colobus.

blocks.orig: Snorkeling and scuba diving at one of the many great reefs.
blocks.html: Scuba diving and snorkelling on any of the many superb reefs.

blocks.orig: Cultural tour: this excursion gives you an insight in the way of life of the local people.
blocks.html: Cultural tour: this outing shows you how local people live their daily lives.

blocks.orig: Mnemba Island tour: snorkeling trip to the most popular snorkeling spot in Zanzibar.
blocks.html: Mnemba Island tour: a snorkelling trip to Zanzibar's most popular snorkelling site.

blocks.orig: A flight from Dar es Salaam to Zanzibar takes only 20 minutes. You can also combine Zanzibar with a safari on the mainland. The distance from Arusha (safari capital) to Zanzibar is about 420 kilometres.
blocks.html: The flight from Dar es Salaam to Zanzibar lasts a mere 20 minutes, and pairing Zanzibar with a mainland safari is easy too. Between Arusha, the safari capital, and Zanzibar lies a distance of roughly 420 kilometres.
